newMustIssues.title: TargetAttributionV2 / OccupancyCompanionV1 admit `logicalPath` in a position their own normative description excludes, and the two admissible spellings of one provider claim mint different run3 identities
newMustIssues.claimUnderTest: logicalPath is a non-authoritative hint ONLY when occupancy is external or unknown AND kind is file or symbol. MUST be null when occupancy=first-party. MUST be null when kind=package.

measured.enforced: the two explicit MUSTs (occupancy=first-party, kind=package) refuse in both schemas and in the atom sidecar guard
measured.notEnforced: the ONLY clause excluding kind=unknown is enforced nowhere: kind=unknown with occupancy=external or unknown and a non-null logicalPath ADMITS in TargetAttributionV2, in OccupancyCompanionV1, and through atom_model.v1 admission; project_companion_to_v2 copies the value mechanically
measured.faultVocabulary: the internal key list contains TARGET_ATTRIBUTION_LOGICAL_PATH_ON_FIRST_PARTY and _ON_PACKAGE only; no key exists for this position
measured.identityConsequence: TargetAttributionV2 identity is raw SHA-256 of C(record). The two spellings measured to 4337e66e444b3d71b8de76248316a2d3de95bc612a798c9de18ed72449f0cbab and 2acc198d05469de051c797508b3a75297289e37be37ecb5240a0e228b61ac16f. That digest is a hostCapture.hostDerivedRefs and ExecutionInputsV1.selectedRefs member, so it reaches C(ExecutionInputsV1), proof.executionInputsDigest, and therefore proof3 / evidence3 / seal3 / run3.

newMustIssues.consequence: One provider observation with undecidable target kind has two admissible encodings that produce two different sealed Run identities. No query answer, finding, verdict or occupancy decision changes, because logicalPath is never read for identity — only the identity of the retained evaluator input changes. That is precisely the independent-replay-across-machines property this contract set closed three times for sibling cases: fact.anchors cardinality (FACT_ANCHOR_CARDINALITY, identity-and-evidence section 3 and native section 1.4), analysis-spec capabilityId spelling (native section 1.4, CB4-SHOULD-2), and TypeScriptConfigGraphV1 node kind (native section 2.2, x-opensip-config-node-kind-law). Each was recorded as a defect on the same reasoning.
newMustIssues.reproducer: probes/pB_target_boundary.py (schema-level, cases B1-B6 plus the measured digest pair) and probes/pB2_model_boundary.py (the actual atom guard and the host projection). Both under /tmp/opensip-architecture-review-env/bin/python -I -B.
newMustIssues.requiredMinimalRemedy: Make the field description and the admission agree, in one of exactly two ways, and state which was chosen. (a) Enforce the stated ONLY: add one allOf branch to each of the two schemas requiring logicalPath null when kind is unknown, and register one internal key (for example TARGET_ATTRIBUTION_LOGICAL_PATH_ON_UNKNOWN_KIND) beside the two existing ones, routed on the existing input-join-invalid / provider-return / EVALUATION.INPUT_REFUSED route with no new DomainDetailCode and no new D9 code. (b) Or withdraw the word ONLY and state that a kind=unknown external or unknown-occupancy record may also carry the hint, accepting that differing hints are different descriptors, exactly as the source-text anchorLaw already states for fact.anchors. Either is a bounded edit; leaving the description and the enforcement disagreeing is not.
newMustIssues.notClaimed: This is not a claim that any admitted Run is semantically wrong, that a query answer changes, or that occupancy reconciliation is unsound. Complete replay, occupancy reconciliation and the C15 conflict laws all behaved correctly in every probe.

newShouldIssues.title: The closing digest law states a universal quantifier that is false of the bundle it annotates, and publishes no machine-readable scope predicate
ownerSelectors: docs/v2/contracts/product-v1/identity-and-evidence.md section 3, 'The closing digest law' ('Every 64-hex field in identity-schemas.v3 has exactly one representation and one retention mode ... a 64-hex field carrying no annotation is inadmissible')

docs/coop/design-corrections/foundation/identity-schemas.v3.json#/x-opensip-digest-domains/standing ('Every 64-hex field in this bundle carries x-opensip-digest; a field without one is not admissible')

measured.referenceEnforcementPredicate: pattern == '^[0-9a-f]{64}(?![\\s\\S])' or $ref == '#/$defs/Hash'; typed-prefix identity fields are outside its scope entirely
measured.prefixToDomainMapInByDomain: absent; no byDomain row carries a prefix key, so the prefix-to-domain resolution exists only in the identity section 3 prose table

newShouldIssues.consequence: A consumer implementing the stated law literally refuses every conforming Plan and Run, because 63 typed-prefix identity occurrences (plan.snapshotId, view.facts[], run.evidenceId, commit-receipt.runId and so on) carry no annotation. The narrower reading the reference actually enforces is correct and the bundle satisfies it with zero residue, but nothing in the normative text or the machine-readable registry says which reading is meant. A blind reconstruction is an explicit obligation of this programme, and this is the first thing such a reader hits.
newShouldIssues.reproducer: probes/pA2_digest_law_refined.py and probes/pA3_digest_scope.py; the reference predicate is read verbatim from check-identity.py.
newShouldIssues.requiredMinimalRemedy: Narrow the quantifier in both places to the fields the law actually governs, and make the scope machine-readable: add a scope key to x-opensip-digest-domains (for example governs: 'every field whose admitted value is a bare 64-hex digest, including a $ref to #/$defs/Hash; a typed-prefix identity field resolves its representation through the domain named by its prefix'), and mirror that one sentence in identity-and-evidence section 3 beside the existing spelling-versus-annotation paragraph.
newShouldIssues.notAFinding: The bare-hex coverage claim itself HOLDS: all 64 bare-hex occurrences carry an effective annotation, including the two that carry it on the non-null oneOf branch (evaluation-deficiency.universe, semantic-grant.principals[].ownerSourceDigest). An earlier run of my own probe reported those two as unannotated; that was my probe reading the annotation at the property rather than at the branch, and it is recorded here as a probe defect, not a design gap.

advisories.title: witnessMalformed is a reportable quarantine condition with no durable representation in the selected carrier_quarantine.reason enum
advisories.why_not_a_should: Read-only recovery is explicitly prohibited from writing any quarantine marker, so no current writer needs the third value, and the two side tables are deliberately preserved byte-identically to the inherited definition (the open dispatch verifies their stored SQL text). independentProbes.class: newly specified retained graph query boundary
independentProbes.claim: graph.neighbors|path|reach are answered only over a Run admitted by complete replay; availability is an observation that may refuse but never grant; endpoint membership, cursor binding, the visited-node cap and the completeness law behave as the contract states; the query-response parity field is the complete owned response.
independentProbes.method: Built a real owner-admitted Run from the semantic fixture and drove the public execute_graph_query entry with my own requests, including at the exact cap boundary.
independentProbes.result: availability purged/expired/corrupt/unavailable all refuse operational-failed / HOST.IO_FAILURE / evidence.{purged,expired,corrupt,missing}; retained and partial answer, with partial backstopped by close_run. A well-formed endpoint outside the vertex domain refuses QUERY.ENDPOINT_UNKNOWN; an admitted vertex with no incident projected fact returns items=0 with traversalCoverage=complete AND disclosed limitations {incoming-search-incomplete, resolution-not-attempted}, so zero rows is not an absence claim. A cursor minted for a different Run refuses QUERY.CURSOR_MISMATCH. Zero-hop at maxVisitedNodes=1 is exactly-at-cap complete (visited 1, countBasis exact); one-edge at the same cap does not enter the target (visited 1, traversalCoverage truncated-bound) and under completeness=required carries top-level termination {class: indeterminate, reasonCodes: [QUERY.COMPLETENESS_UNMET], runId}; under best-effort it carries none. The parity projection returns query-response byte-equal to the complete owned GraphQueryResponseV1, all four scalars plus termination-class as exact projections of its context, completenessMet true exactly when countBasis == exact in both directions, advisory const false, and refuses a response/termination pair that does not agree (QUERY_SURFACE_RESPONSE_TERMINATION_MISMATCH). command-inventory query parityFields are exactly the six section-8 fields.

independentProbes.class: fully reminted false-result graph — structural admission versus semantic authority
independentProbes.claim: A structurally perfect, internally hash-consistent graph carrying a false semantic result passes structural owner admission and fails complete replay, and the public graph boundary is not the structural API.
independentProbes.method: Took the admitted positive Run and applied three independent semantic mutations (verdict flipped, one retained predicate-proof value flipped, one execution deficiency dropped), then reminted proof-bundle -> semantic-evidence -> evaluation-seal -> run so every enclosing identity was recomputed and the graph was internally consistent.
independentProbes.result: All three produce a DIFFERENT RunId (a true remint). All three ADMIT under identity-model.v3.open_run_closure. All three REFUSE under identity-model.v3.close_run with EVALUATOR_COMPLETE_PROOF_REPLAY. All three REFUSE at execute_graph_query, which calls close_run, with operational-failed / HOST.IO_FAILURE / evidence.corrupt. Separately, admit_cache_entry calls close_run FIRST and then resolves the key's references through the Run's own closure, so a cache hit cannot bypass complete replay; cache_key construction reads no bytes.
independentProbes.finding: verified; the structural API is not semantic authority, and there is no cached-payload bypass

limitations: This is a design review of frozen bytes. It qualifies no product, compiler, provider, host, filesystem, OS, cryptographic primitive or platform, and it authorizes no implementation.

Every reference checker I ran operates over synthetic trusted inputs. Passing them establishes that the reference models implement the stated joins; it establishes nothing about a real TypeScript compiler, a real rustc, real fsync, real SQLite crash behaviour, real process isolation or real lock contention. All 54 commit-recovery cases and every one of the 32 gates remain unperformed product obligations.

Synthetic TCB observations throughout the security, native and integration models are asserted assumptions, not proof of enforcement. Signature verification, ACL and lstat results, platform truth-table values and provider returns are all supplied, not measured.
I did not perform, and do not claim, a blind consumer reconstruction. A separate NEW blind session follows under the original charter and receives only the normative kit.

My reading is complete over the documents listed in contractsReadCompletely and complete over the records of the machine-readable files listed in machineDataTraversedCompletely. It is not a per-predicate proof of every prose sentence in the 736 MB subject, and the historical reviews/ tree (11,545 files, 718 MB) was verified by hash but not read.

The prototype source pins in implementation-planning-sources.v1.json name files in a separate repository at commit a62509d623173155d0946e9f5d5ca90c839893e0. Those files are not members of this subject, so their 44 digests are not independently verifiable from these bytes, and I did not execute the prototype.

The carrier correction's executed controls C1-C18 are cited by scratch/ paths that are not retained in the subject (advisory A-3). I re-ran check-carrier-v3.py by reconstructing its expected runtime layout from frozen bytes; that reproduces the validator, not the original C1-C18 measurements.

Two of my own probes initially reported false positives, both recorded rather than hidden: probe A read a digest annotation at the property rather than at its non-null oneOf branch, and my first graph-query request helper omitted schemaFamily, so an early run of probe C/D refused at request validation and its D3 rows were not evidence about the graph boundary. Both were corrected and re-run.

D9's later published successor artifact carrying the host-invariant faultCause is a carried implementation obligation of the D9 unit. I treat it as such, not as a design-level blocker, consistent with the contract's own disclosure.
